data.title: CANADA STOCKS-TSX futures slip as lower oil, gold prices weigh; retail sales data eyed
data.description:
Nov 20 (Reuters) - Futures tracking Canada's blue-chip stocks fell on Friday as lower oil and gold prices weighed on sentiment, while investors awaited domestic retail sales data due later in the day.

December futures on the S&P/TSX 60 index were down 0.36% at 05:32 a.m. ET (1032 GMT).

* Brent crude shed about 2%, heading for a third straight weekly decline on strong exports from the Middle East despite Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia's capital Riyadh and reports of tanker disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz

* Gold prices, meanwhile, were headed for their worst week in eight months, as expectations of a Federal Reserve interest-rate hike in December supported the dollar

* The spotlight is also on domestic retail sales data, due at 08:30 ET, which will be closely watched for signals on the health of Canadian consumers

* Separately, Canada is still seeking a temporary deal to ease US tariffs on its goods, though Washington has shown little willingness to budge, Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc told an advisory committee on Thursday, sources said

* US futures fell and stock markets across the globe tumbled after Anthropic's IPO failed to restore investors' faith in the AI sector

* On Thursday, Canada's main stock index fell for a sixth straight day as a selloff in gold extended, with metal mining and technology shares pacing broad-based declines

* In company news, Bausch + Lomb ( BLCO ) said its experimental eye-drop treatment failed to significantly reduce pain during the first 24 hours after laser eye surgery in a mid-stage study

data.title: High AI Anxiety Blunts Asian Stock Markets
data.description:
05:54 AM EST, 11/20/2026 (MT Newswires) -- Asian stock markets on Friday took cues from Wall Street's overnight sell-off of tech shares, as traders again backed away from AI- and semiconductor-related issues.

The Thursday listing on Wall Street of Anthropic's (ANT) relatively successful IPO did not quell investor concerns that the AI-sector faces huge capital outlays but uncertain revenue, and possible government regulation.

Hong Kong, Shanghai and Tokyo finished in the red Friday, while Taiwan's TWSE index fell 6.2%, and Seoul's semiconductor-laden KOSPI index declined 5.2%.

In Japan, the Nikkei 225 opened lower and fell to the bell, finishing down 5.1%.

The benchmark Nikkei 225 fell 3,007.56 to 56,436.65, as losing issues outnumbered gainers 213 to 11.

Leading the upside was insurer Tokio Marine, up 2% after reporting earnings, while tech-financier SoftBank declined nearly 15%.

In economic news, Japan's core consumer price index -- which excludes fresh food -- rose 2.2% on year last month, following a 2.1% rise in September, reported the Bank of Japan.

In Hong Kong, the Hang Seng Index opened lower and could not recover, closing down 1.9% as tech and property shares retreated.

The broad gauge Hang Seng dropped 430.82 to 22,410.8, as losing issues outnumbered gainers 84 to six. The Hang Seng TECH Index lost 3.8% on the day, while the Mainland Properties Index fell 2.1%.

Leading the upside was e-commerce colossus Alibaba ( BABA ) , gaining 3.5%, while internet-and-video giant NetEase slumped 18%, with both moves following earnings reports.

On the mainland, the Shanghai Composite fell 1.2% to 3,533.79.

In economic news, the People's Bank of China kept its key lending rates unchanged, at 3% for one-year loans, and 3.5% for three-year loans.

On the other regional exchanges, the Australian ASX 200 declined 1.6%; the Singapore Straits Times Index fell 2.1%, and the Thai Set lost 1.3%. In late trading in Mumbai, the Sensex was up 1.1%

The MSCI All Country Asia Pacific Index fell 3.2% on the day.

data.title: VisionWave Holdings Acquires Critical Minerals Intelligence Platform, Targeting Near-Term Commercialization of Defense Supply-Chain Intelligence
data.description:
Platform designed to address growing demand for critical-mineral pricing intelligence, geopolitical supply-risk monitoring, regulatory compliance and procurement transparency

Initial focus on tungsten and antimony, with potential expansion into rare earths, semiconductors and other defense-critical materials

VisionWave ( VWAV ) intends to pursue near-term revenue opportunities through subscription-based intelligence services, compliance documentation and transaction-related services

WEST HOLLYWOOD, Calif., Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- VisionWave Holdings, Inc. ( VWAV ) (“VisionWave” or the “Company”), a technology company developing advanced defense, autonomous systems and artificial intelligence solutions, today announced the acquisition of the Critical Minerals Intelligence Platform (“CMIP”), a specialized technology platform designed to provide market intelligence, supply-chain transparency, regulatory screening and procurement-related information for strategically important critical minerals.

The agreement with Litial Ltd was signed on November 18, 2026, and the acquisition has not yet closed. If completed, the acquisition would mark VisionWave's ( VWAV ) entry into the defense-industrial supply-chain intelligence market and is intended to establish a new commercial technology offering with the potential to generate recurring revenue through subscriptions, compliance-related services and transaction-based fees.

Unlike technologies requiring extensive hardware development or manufacturing infrastructure before commercialization, CMIP's software- and data-driven architecture is designed to support deployment through digital services and enterprise workflows.

According to the technology developer's materials, CMIP includes a browser-based minimum viable product (MVP) supporting benchmark monitoring, counterparty screening and compliance-document generation. VisionWave ( VWAV ) intends, following the closing of the acquisition, to evaluate these capabilities for commercial deployment and pursue initial revenue opportunities following technical, cybersecurity and regulatory validation.

The platform initially focuses on tungsten and antimony, two materials of strategic importance to defense, aerospace and advanced manufacturing. VisionWave ( VWAV ) also sees potential to extend the platform to other critical minerals, specialized industrial materials and defense-related components.

Addressing a Strategic Challenge in Defense and Industrial Supply Chains

Critical minerals have become increasingly important to national security, defense readiness, industrial resilience and international trade.

Tungsten is used in applications including aerospace components, wear-resistant materials, cutting equipment and ammunition. Antimony is used in specialized industrial and defense-related applications.

Both minerals appear on the United States' 2025 Critical Minerals List and the European Union's critical raw materials list, reflecting their economic importance and exposure to supply-chain vulnerabilities.

Global supply chains for these materials face several structural challenges:

  • Geopolitical supply concentration: Significant production and processing capacity is concentrated in a limited number of countries, creating potential exposure to geopolitical developments and trade restrictions.
  • Export controls and sanctions: International restrictions can affect material availability, supplier eligibility and cross-border transactions.
  • Pricing complexity: Market participants must navigate different material grades, delivery conditions, geographic markets and pricing methodologies.
  • Limited supply-chain visibility: Identifying the origin, processing history and chain of custody of strategically important materials can be challenging.
  • Fragmented procurement information: Pricing, counterparty verification, regulatory screening and material provenance are often handled through separate systems.

China's export restrictions on antimony-related products in 2024 and selected tungsten-related products in 2025 have further highlighted the strategic importance of supply-chain intelligence.

VisionWave ( VWAV ) believes these developments create an opportunity for technology platforms capable of combining market data, regulatory information, supplier intelligence and transaction documentation to support more informed procurement and risk-management decisions.

CMIP: An Integrated Critical Minerals Intelligence Platform

CMIP is designed as a specialized market-intelligence and workflow platform rather than simply a commodity trading application.

Its architecture brings together four complementary capabilities intended to help organizations understand critical-mineral markets, evaluate counterparties, document transactions and monitor supply-chain exposure.

1. Critical Minerals Pricing and Market Intelligence

CMIP includes a proposed benchmark pricing framework covering tungsten ammonium paratungstate (APT), antimony trioxide and antimony metal.

The framework is designed to support structured price monitoring, documented pricing methodologies and market comparisons.

By combining market pricing information with other supply-chain and transaction data, CMIP aims to support procurement planning, commercial negotiations and material sourcing decisions.

2. Regulatory Compliance and Sanctions Intelligence

The platform incorporates automated counterparty-screening workflows designed to reference relevant sanctions and restricted-party information, including U.S., European Union and United Nations sources.

Its compliance infrastructure is intended to support counterparty identity and sanctions screening, export-control information workflows, documentation of screening results and regulatory risk indicators, and compliance-related records and audit trails.

These capabilities are intended to assist compliance professionals and procurement organizations, rather than replace required legal determinations or regulatory approvals.

3. Controlled Counterparty and Transaction Network

CMIP includes a proposed closed over-the-counter network designed to connect prequalified commercial participants in strategically important materials markets.

The network architecture contemplates business-identity verification, sanctions screening, controlled participant access and structured transaction workflows.

VisionWave ( VWAV ) believes this approach could help support more transparent and accountable interactions among mineral producers, processors, traders, industrial buyers and defense-related procurement organizations.

4. Material Provenance and Supply-Chain Traceability

A central element of CMIP's long-term strategy is the development of structured data linking materials to their origins, processing history, counterparties and transaction records.

This information could enable organizations to evaluate where a critical material originated, which suppliers and intermediaries handled it, whether counterparties are subject to restrictions, and how geopolitical developments affect sourcing risks.

VisionWave ( VWAV ) believes the ability to connect material provenance, regulatory information and procurement intelligence could become an important differentiating capability as the platform develops and accumulates appropriately licensed transaction data.

Near-Term Revenue Opportunities and Commercialization Strategy

VisionWave ( VWAV ) intends to prioritize the commercialization of CMIP through three complementary revenue channels:

  • Annual subscriptions: Recurring fees for access to critical-minerals pricing intelligence, supplier-risk information, compliance tools and related services.
  • Transaction-related fees: Potential revenue from facilitating transactions through the platform's controlled counterparty network.
  • Compliance documentation services: Fees associated with screening records, documentation workflows and transaction-related compliance support.

The platform developer's proposed commercial model contemplates annual enterprise subscriptions ranging from approximately $25,000 to $75,000, transaction fees of approximately 0.25%–0.5% of matched transactions, and compliance-documentation fees of approximately $500–$2,000 per service.

These figures represent proposed pricing assumptions rather than established customer contracts or verified historical revenue. VisionWave ( VWAV ) has not independently validated these assumptions, and there can be no assurance that any customer will purchase services at these or any other prices.

VisionWave ( VWAV ) intends to pursue early commercial opportunities using the platform's existing software capabilities while evaluating additional functionality, regulatory requirements and customer needs.

The Company's objective is to establish an initial revenue-generating business and subsequently expand the platform's customer base, data coverage and integration with VisionWave's ( VWAV ) broader intelligence technologies.

Commercial deployment and the timing of any revenue generation remain subject to technical validation, customer adoption and applicable regulatory requirements.

Potential Integration with StratumAI: Toward Defense Supply-Chain Intelligence

VisionWave ( VWAV ) intends to evaluate connecting CMIP with its StratumAI intelligence architecture to develop more advanced defense supply-chain intelligence capabilities.

The proposed integration would seek to combine critical-minerals data, regulatory information, geopolitical developments and AI-supported analysis to create a more comprehensive defense-industrial intelligence capability.

Potential applications include supplier-risk monitoring, commodity price and availability intelligence, sanctioned-party detection, geopolitical supply-risk analysis, provenance review, alternative-source identification and procurement alerts.

The Company believes this approach could extend the application of AI-driven intelligence beyond physical sensing and autonomous systems into the materials and industrial supply chains that support defense technologies.

Over time, VisionWave ( VWAV ) may evaluate expanding the platform beyond tungsten and antimony to other strategically important materials and components, including rare earth elements, gallium, germanium, graphite, titanium, specialized alloys, semiconductors, electronic components and defense manufacturing inputs.

Such expansion would be subject to additional technology development, data availability, regulatory requirements and commercial validation.

Acquisition Terms and Strategic Commercial Support

Under the acquisition agreement, VisionWave ( VWAV ) has agreed to acquire CMIP from Litial Ltd for $11 million in deferred consideration, to be evidenced by an unsecured, subordinated, non-interest-bearing promissory note to be delivered at closing.

The purchase consideration is payable in two installments of $5.5 million on the first and second anniversaries of closing, subject to defined revenue milestones.

Both installments are contingent upon CMIP generating qualifying revenue of at least $500,000 during the first three months following closing and an additional $1 million during the subsequent three months. If either milestone is not achieved, both installments are forfeited. The closing of the acquisition is subject to customary conditions and to VisionWave's ( VWAV ) receipt of an independent third-party valuation of CMIP supporting the purchase price, which has not yet been delivered and which may not be waived by either party. Either party may terminate the agreement if the closing has not occurred by December 31, 2026. There can be no assurance that the valuation will support the purchase price or that the acquisition will be completed.

The acquisition is structured without an upfront cash payment or issuance of VisionWave ( VWAV ) common shares.

VisionWave ( VWAV ) also entered into a two-year strategic engagement agreement with DNE International FZ LLC to provide advisory and administrative support relating to CMIP's commercial development and operational planning.

DNE's $3.8 million contractual compensation is evidenced by a subordinated, unsecured, non-interest-bearing promissory note and is subject to the same CMIP revenue milestones and other contractual conditions, and will be cancelled if the CMIP acquisition does not close by March 31, 2027.

The Company believes the transaction structure preserves equity capital while aligning the acquisition consideration and related advisory compensation with defined commercial performance. Additional information regarding these agreements is included in the Company's Current Report on Form 8-K filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.

Additional Acquisition of AI-Powered Video Intelligence Technology

Separately, on November 18, 2026, VisionWave ( VWAV ) completed the $4 million acquisition of MoreSpeed, an AI-powered forensic video search technology, from SofTech Resources Limited.

MoreSpeed is designed to accelerate the identification of relevant persons, vehicles and events within large video repositories through an AI-based search and prioritization architecture.

Developer-supplied benchmarks reported median search acceleration of approximately 18.8 times against the tested baseline, which VisionWave ( VWAV ) has not independently verified and which remain subject to the Company's post-closing verification of the delivered assets.

VisionWave ( VWAV ) intends to evaluate MoreSpeed for potential integration with its existing xCalibre video analytics and broader intelligence technology portfolio.

The acquisition consideration is payable through an unsecured, non-interest-bearing promissory note due on the first anniversary of closing, subject to contractual protections. Unlike the CMIP consideration, the MoreSpeed payment obligation is not contingent on future revenue.

Management Commentary

Douglas Davis, Chief Executive Officer and Executive Chairman of VisionWave Holdings ( VWAV ), commented:

“Critical minerals are becoming an increasingly important component of national security, defense readiness and industrial resilience. The challenge is no longer simply obtaining these materials, but understanding where they originate, who controls their supply, how geopolitical developments affect availability, and whether procurement decisions can be supported by reliable and transparent information.

“With the planned acquisition of CMIP, we expect to enter a strategically important intelligence market that complements our broader defense technology vision.

“We believe the opportunity extends beyond conventional commodity pricing. Our objective is to bring together market intelligence, regulatory screening, supply-chain provenance and AI-supported analysis into an integrated environment that can help organizations better understand critical-material sourcing risks.

“Importantly, our near-term priority is commercialization. The platform's existing software capabilities and proposed subscription, transaction and compliance-service revenue models provide a foundation for pursuing early commercial opportunities without requiring the extensive manufacturing infrastructure associated with hardware-based products.

“CMIP also creates a potential new intelligence domain for StratumAI, allowing us to explore applications in defense procurement, supplier-risk analysis, geopolitical monitoring and strategic materials intelligence.

“We see the initial focus on tungsten and antimony as a starting point, with the longer-term potential to address a broader range of critical minerals, electronic components and industrial supply-chain dependencies.

“We have structured the acquisition without upfront cash consideration or equity issuance, with the purchase price tied to defined commercial revenue milestones.

“Our strategy is to acquire and develop differentiated intellectual property that can address meaningful operational challenges, generate commercial opportunities and create long-term value for VisionWave ( VWAV ) and its shareholders.”

About VisionWave Holdings, Inc. ( VWAV )

VisionWave Holdings, Inc. ( VWAV ) is a technology company developing dual-use unmanned systems, autonomous capabilities, and advanced sensing solutions for defense, security, and commercial applications. Its portfolio includes the VARAN unmanned ground vehicle (UGV) platform and a suite of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and drone solutions, supported by sensing, perception, and autonomy technologies. Through technology development and strategic partnerships, VisionWave ( VWAV ) aims to deliver integrated ground and aerial systems that enhance situational awareness, support operational missions, and reduce personnel exposure to risk across military and civilian environments. For more information, visit https://www.vwav.inc.

data.title: Kpler completes $1.5bn+ Sixth Street investment and continues accelerating growth
data.description:
Investment backs Kpler's bold ambition to shape the future of global trade intelligence

LONDON, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Kpler, a leading provider of global physical trade intelligence data and analytics, today announced the completion of a previously announced investment by Sixth Street, which has acquired over $1.5bn worth of shares in the company. Insight Partners, an investor since 2022, remains a shareholder alongside Kpler's founders François Cazor and Jean Maynier and the management team. Five Arrows has exited its investment.

The investment brings Sixth Street on board as a partner for Kpler's next phase of growth, supporting the company's ambitions for the coming years. Kpler remains independent, with its leadership, strategy, and day-to-day operations unchanged.

Profitable and experiencing strong growth, Kpler is focused on continuously enriching its proprietary datasets, advancing its technology, and developing new solutions for customers across energy, trading, insurance, maritime, logistics, the public sector, and beyond. At the heart of this strategy is a commitment to solving real problems alongside customers, using Kpler's unparalleled visibility of global trade to help them make better decisions and trade smarter.

Kpler's growth has been driven by continued investment in technology, data, and strategic acquisitions, including MarineTraffic, the globally recognised vessel tracking platform acquired in 2023. More recently, the acquisition of Spire's maritime business expanded Kpler's satellite AIS capabilities, while its partnership with Airbus brought Earth observation imagery into its vessel tracking offering. Together, these investments strengthen the quality, depth and reach of Kpler's intelligence, with further innovation planned in the coming months.

Since pioneering LNG cargo tracking in 2014, Kpler has become a global authority on commodity and maritime intelligence. Behind its success is a powerful combination of cutting-edge technology, high-quality proprietary data, an extensive global collection network, and some of the industry's best talent.

With a team approaching 1,000 people across 41 countries, Kpler continues to invest in AI, new products, and even higher-quality data, while pursuing strategic acquisitions that strengthen its capabilities and open up new opportunities for its customers.

Mark Cunningham, CEO of Kpler, said:

"Kpler has always succeeded by challenging convention and finding better ways to solve hard problems. Twelve years on, we're a profitable, fast-growing company that others benchmark themselves against. But our ambitions go much further. In a world of shifting trade routes, supply chains, and energy markets, customers need intelligence they can trust. We intend to lead in every market we enter, and that takes bold thinking, speed, and the determination to keep raising the bar.

"With Sixth Street joining us, we have an investor that shares our ambition and believes in our long-term potential. I want to thank our clients and partners for their trust, and above all our exceptional team, whose talent and determination have brought Kpler to where it is today. They will be central to everything we achieve in the years ahead."

Mike McGinn, Partner and Co-Head of Growth, and Henry Davies, Managing Director at Sixth Street, shared:

"We believe Kpler has the ambition and capabilities to shape the future of global trade intelligence, and we're delighted to partner with Mark, François, Jean, and the rest of their exceptional team to help realise that vision. The opportunity goes well beyond serving today's markets: it is about expanding what customers can see, understand, and act on across global trade. We share the team's conviction in the scale of that opportunity and are committed to supporting the innovation, strategic acquisitions, and global expansion that will bring it to life."

About Kpler

Kpler is a leading intelligence platform for global physical trade, bringing transparency to the flows and forces shaping markets, economies, and security worldwide. Combining proprietary data, advanced analytics, AI-powered technologies, and expert market analysis, Kpler transforms complex global trade information into actionable intelligence. With visibility across more than 40 markets, including energy, dry bulk, power, and maritime transport, Kpler helps businesses and governments navigate volatility, manage risk, and uncover opportunities across global markets.

Founded in 2014, Kpler pioneered LNG cargo tracking and has since grown into a leading provider of trade intelligence across commodity and shipping markets. Through its two complementary platforms, Kpler and MarineTraffic, Kpler delivers the data, insights, and transparency needed to better understand global trade flows and the forces shaping markets worldwide.

About Sixth Street

Sixth Street is a global multi-strategy private capital investment firm with more than $140 billion in assets under management and committed capital as of June 30, 2026. Founded in 2009, Sixth Street is dynamic by design, pairing the flexibility of its long-term capital with a focus on identifying the best relative risk-reward opportunities in any asset class, any industry, around the globe. With more than 750 team members across 14 offices worldwide, Sixth Street is built as One Team for one purpose: to deliver investing excellence for its capital partners, companies and management teams. For more information and additional disclosures, visit www.sixthstreet.com, and follow Sixth Street on LinkedIn.

data.title: Fed's Paulson says understanding, not guidance, drives effective communication
data.description:
NEW YORK, Nov 19 (Reuters) - Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia President Anna Paulson said on Thursday central bank communications work better when officials and the public understand one another, rather than when Fed officials provide explicit comments about what they think lies ahead.

For the Fed, "understanding matters more than the specific ways we communicate," Paulson said in the text of a speech to be delivered before a gathering held by the Money Marketeers of New York University.

"When we understand each other, we don't need to say as much when new data arrive," she said, adding, "You can anticipate how we'll respond, and we can act in ways that are steady and, for the most part, predictable."

WARSH'S COMMUNICATION OVERHAUL

Paulson's views on Fed communications come as the central bank has been overhauling how it explains its actions to the public. Under new Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh, the Fed has shortened its Federal Open Market Committee policy statement and has launched a special task force to weigh how the Fed should communicate its actions and views.

At the same time, Warsh has, in contrast to other recent Fed leaders, stepped almost entirely away from providing any guidance about the interest-rate outlook.

But even as Warsh has pulled back, many of his colleagues on the central bank have continued to provide regular updates on where they think interest-rate policy is heading and how the economy is faring.

Paulson did not offer any comments about the near-term outlook for interest-rate policy, as the central bank approaches its December 8-9 Federal Open Market Committee meeting, where it is widely expected to hike rates by a quarter percentage point, to between 4% and 4.25%.

Paulson said in her remarks that understanding how the Fed reacts to incoming data is particularly important.

"Communication works best when it builds a shared understanding of the reaction function, and that credibility is essential, because people act on messages they trust," she said.

Paulson said an understanding of what the Fed is doing and why helped markets navigate the Fed's decision to hold rates steady in late October after boosting them in September and signaling more hikes were in the works.

"In October, markets expected further tightening, so the pause did not leave policy behind where it needed to be," she said. "A shared understanding of the reaction function allowed policy to move deliberately and gave people time to adjust, without the risk that a pause was mistaken for a stop."

(Reporting by Michael S. Derby in New York; Editing by Matthew Lewis)

data.title: US STOCKS-Wall St futures slip as Anthropic debut fails to reassure AI investors
data.description:
(For a Reuters live blog on U.S., UK and European stock markets, click or type LIVE/ in a news window.)

* Futures down: Dow 0.2%, S&P 500 0.76%, Nasdaq 1.63%

* Anthropic down 6.5% a day after its debut

* Gap gains on Old Navy recovery

Nov 20 (Reuters) - US stock futures fell on Friday as Anthropic shares retreated after a blockbuster debut, dashing hopes that the high-profile listing could steady an AI trade rattled by growth and valuation concerns, while hawkish signals from Federal Reserve officials this week also weighed on sentiment.

Anthropic shares slid 6.8% in premarket trading after surging more than 17% on Thursday in their highly anticipated market debut. The stock began trading more than 34% above its offer price of $83.

The Claude chatbot creator's IPO was seen as a key test of investor confidence in the AI theme after a bruising few weeks for the sector. Concerns over potentially slower data center expansion, higher borrowing costs and the departure of Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO Jensen Huang have intensified fears about returns on massive spending.

The Nasdaq was 13.6% below its record closing high of October 6.

Among hyperscalers, Amazon ( AMZN ), Meta, and Microsoft ( MSFT ) declined more than 1.8% each, while Alphabet was muted. Amazon ( AMZN ) and Alphabet are among Anthropic's biggest investors.

Chipmakers were lower, with Nvidia ( NVDA ) down 2.6%, while Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ), Broadcom ( AVGO ), Marvell ( MRVL ) , and Micron lost between 3.5% and 5.5%.

Neoclouds CoreWeave and Nebius also dropped more than 5% each.

Data center stocks IREN ( IREN ), Applied Digital ( APLD ) and Core Scientific ( CORZ ) fell between 2.8% and 4%.

At 4:57 a.m. ET, Dow E-minis were down 99 points, or 0.2%, and S&P 500 E-minis were down 54.5 points, or 0.76%. Nasdaq 100 E-minis were down 434 points, or 1.63%.

Wall Street's main indexes were on track for their steepest weekly decline since April 2025, when US President Donald Trump announced Liberation Day tariffs.

The selloff in AI-linked stocks has largely overshadowed a strong earnings season.

Of the 462 companies in the S&P 500 to have reported results through Wednesday, 83.5% reported earnings above analyst expectations, according to an analysis from Tajinder Dhillon, head of earnings and equity research at LSEG Data and Analytics.

INFLATION, FED IN FOCUS

Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia President Anna Paulson said on Thursday the Fed will need to raise interest rates again because inflation is too high, while arguing that shared understanding matters more than explicit guidance on the rate outlook.

Markets are pricing in a 98.4% chance of an interest rate hike from the central bank at its next meeting in December, according to CME Group's FedWatch tool.

Next week's personal consumption expenditures (PCE) figures will provide further clarity on the Fed's monetary policy path after a hotter-than-expected October inflation report last week.

Brent crude prices fell 1.6% and were heading for a third straight weekly loss on expectations of a supply surplus, with crude shipments through the Strait of Hormuz returning to roughly prewar levels.

Markets were also assessing the outcome of the meeting between Trump and his Chinese and Russian counterparts Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin, after the leaders issued a joint peace declaration that made no mention of the conflict between the US and Iran.

Among other movers, apparel retailer Gap rose 2.5% after its Old Navy brand posted better-than-expected quarterly sales.

(Reporting by Utkarsh Hathi in Bengaluru; Editing by Maju Samuel)

data.title: GLOBAL MARKETS-Stocks slide as AI selloff deepens, Asia set for worst week since 2020
data.description:
(Updates throughout for European session, adds chart)

* Asian stocks on track for worst week since COVID hit

* Anthropic's historic debut fails to revive faith in AI trade

* US futures fall after S&P 500 drops for six straight sessions

By Harry Robertson, Jiaxing Li and Rae Wee

LONDON/HONG KONG/SINGAPORE, Nov 20 (Reuters) - Stock markets stumbled around the world on Friday after Anthropic's IPO failed to restore investors' faith in the AI sector, with Asian shares heading for their worst week since 2020, US futures falling and a gauge of global equities set for its seventh straight daily decline.

Government bonds rallied as investors sought safe-haven assets.

Shares of Anthropic, the world's first publicly traded frontier AI company, jumped as it launched the biggest IPO in history on Thursday, although they pared gains later in the session.

The debut did little to revive excitement over the broader AI theme, however, as investors continued to question whether the huge amounts of spending would deliver returns.

"It was far from the euphoria needed to inject new energy into the AI trade," said Johan Javeus, senior economist at Swedish bank SEB.

The STOXX 600 gauge of European stocks fell 1.5% in morning trading, down 5% from a record high on November 12.

MSCI's world index of stocks fell for a seventh straight session, the longest losing streak since 2023.

The MSCI index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan tumbled and has sunk 8% this week, its worst performance since the COVID pandemic in March 2020.

Nvidia's ( NVDA ) blowout earnings earlier in the week and Anthropic's IPO have both failed to restore confidence, said Charu Chanana, chief investment strategist at bank and investment firm Saxo.

"The market is no longer looking for proof of AI demand alone," she said. "It wants evidence that the extraordinary spending across the ecosystem can generate sustainable returns."

In the US, futures for the tech-focused Nasdaq 100 fell 1.5% after the index dropped more than 2% on Thursday. The Nasdaq is now down around 15% since hitting a record high in early October.

S&P 500 futures were in the red after the index fell for a sixth straight session on Thursday. A seven-day run of declines would be the worst losing streak since the pandemic.

The VIX index of expected volatility on Wall Street stocks jumped and traded at its highest since March on Friday.

Adding to the unease, a report on AMD from a media outlet associated with short-selling fund Hunterbrook Capital raised concerns that the chipmaker's ties to Chinese entities, some linked to blacklisted firms, could draw greater US regulatory scrutiny to the sector.

"No one headline drove the roll, though some pointed to an AMD short report which tapered overall sentiment," said Goldman Sachs analysts in a trading note.

"Overall, it just felt like more questions than answers out there today with most wondering what gets this tape to feel better?"

All of that has piled further pressure on the AI trade, already battered in recent weeks by Jensen Huang's departure from Nvidia ( NVDA ) and growing anti-data-centre sentiment exemplified by the Democrats' sweep of the US midterm elections.

Japan's Nikkei tumbled 5%. Taiwanese shares were down 17% for the week, their biggest weekly decline since 1990.

Despite the sharp drop in stocks, however, equity markets remain up for the year after a blistering rally in the first half on AI optimism.

TREASURIES RALLY AS INVESTORS TAKE COVER

US Treasuries rallied as stocks took a beating, sending investors towards assets deemed safe havens.

The yield on benchmark 10-year Treasury notes fell for a fifth straight session, to below 5%, while German 10-year bond yields fell 7 bps, the most since mid-October . Bond yields move inversely to prices.

Meanwhile, the US dollar held steady at around its highest level in 20 months, also garnering support from growing expectations of a more hawkish Federal Reserve.

Fed funds futures imply that a quarter-point rate hike next month is essentially locked in, according to CME Group's FedWatch tool.

Oil prices were steady, with Brent crude futures trading at $90 a barrel and on track for a third week of declines.

(Reporting by Harry Robertson in London, Jiaxing Li in Hong Kong and Rae Wee in Singapore; Editing by Edwina Gibbs, Christian Schmollinger, Lincoln Feast and Xevi Fontdegloria)

data.title: Democrats open probe into Nvidia influence on US Megaspeed investigation
data.description:
NEW YORK, Nov 20 (Reuters) - Democratic lawmakers have opened a probe into what influence Nvidia was able to wield over a US Commerce Department investigation of cloud company Megaspeed for possible illegal diversion of chips to China, according to a letter reviewed by Reuters.

In the November 19 letter to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, the House Democrats said they wanted to know "whether the department allowed a major American corporation that is financially and personally linked to the Trump administration to interfere with enforcement activity."

Singapore-based Megaspeed has attracted public attention since news broke that former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had an affair with former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, whom US authorities suspect of being a Chinese spy. Jensen Huang resigned on Thursday. China has denied Alice Huang is a spy.

Megaspeed, an Nvidia partner that operates data centers, has been under US investigation for two years, the departments of Commerce and Justice said this week. They said Commerce investigators requested records from Nvidia in May 2025 about sales to the company and, with Singaporean authorities, conducted an on-site inspection in June 2025 at Megaspeed and interviewed Alice Huang.

In August 2025, Nvidia contacted Commerce employees directly and requested a meeting with one of them, a Commerce official told Reuters, referring to the investigators. Nvidia told them Commerce Under Secretary Jeffrey Kessler said the company could communicate with the employees.

"The American public and Congress deserve a full accounting of what happened, " US Representatives Gregory Meeks, ranking member of the House Committee on Foreign Affairs, and Sydney Kamlager-Dove of California wrote in the letter, which requested answers and relevant documents by December 1.

"BIS conducts all enforcement strictly by the book," a spokesperson for the department's Bureau of Industry and Security said in a statement. "BIS enforces aggressively across the board, including with respect to chip smuggling."

Megaspeed said it complies with all applicable laws, including US export control requirements.

An Nvidia spokesperson said that, as an American company it consults with department officials to answer questions, provide information and request their guidance and instructions.

"We look forward to engaging with Congress on this matter," the statement said.

(Editing by Stephen Coates)

MANCHESTER, England, Nov 20 (Reuters) - A drone operator who filmed Manchester United's ( MANU ) training session this week has apologised for what he called a "total error of judgment" and removed the footage from his YouTube channel.

The footage, filmed at United's Carrington training ground during new manager Mauricio Pochettino's first training session on Thursday, was uploaded online under the username "CC OVERVIEW".

In a statement posted on his YouTube channel on Friday, the drone operator said that while the flight was legal under drone regulations, filming the session had been "unethical".

"My aim was to picture Mauricio Pochettino in his United training kit for the supporters to see for the first time," he said.

"I fully accept it was unethical on my part. I would like to apologise to Manchester United ( MANU ), Mauricio Pochettino and the players for my actions and sincerely hope those actions do not affect the outcome of any match."

The operator added that he had wrongly assumed only warm-up activities would be visible and that the training session would be open to various media outlets.

He also said neither Liverpool nor any other football club had been involved in his decision to film at Carrington.

"The video has been removed from my channel," he said.

Pochettino arrived from the U.S. men's national team this week after United sacked Michael Carrick, and faces an immediate test with a trip to Liverpool on Sunday.

United are languishing 18th in the league table after winning just one of their 10 games. Liverpool are fourth.

data.title: FOREX-Dollar near 19-month high, set for 4th weekly gain as AI worries fuel haven bid
data.description:
(Updates pricing in European morning)

* Dollar index near strongest since early April 2025

* Markets debating size, not likelihood, of December Fed hike

* Yen firms after Japan core inflation hits 2.2%

By Li Gu and Rae Wee

SHANGHAI/SINGAPORE, Nov 20 (Reuters) - The dollar was steady on Friday, and was on track to rise for the fourth straight week as expectations of further Federal Reserve tightening underpinned the US currency and jitters over the AI trade sent investors fleeing to safe-haven assets.

The dollar index was perched near the 103.8 level, around its strongest since early April 2025. The weeks-long rally accelerated on November 10, when hotter-than-expected US inflation data reinforced bets that the Federal Reserve would tighten policy and Fed Governor Christopher Waller said a 50-basis-point hike in December should be considered.

The strong dollar also comes amid weak equity sentiment, with AI spending concerns dragging the S&P 500 lower for six straight sessions. The index is down about 5% so far this week, and Anthropic's record market debut on Thursday did little to revive investor confidence.

Anthropic notched a valuation of about $2 trillion in its Nasdaq debut on Thursday, edging past SpaceX's June listing and capping a volatile stretch for the AI sector that tested Wall Street's appetite for the technology.

"Risk aversion intensified, supporting the safe-haven dollar and driving demand for US Treasuries," OCBC analysts said in a note. "Investors continued to unwind crowded positions and reassess the macro outlook as Anthropic's record IPO sharpened scrutiny of stretched AI valuations and financing risks."

The US 10-year Treasury yield fell to a one-week low of just over 5% and is down more than 14 basis points on the week.

Adding to the dollar's strength were hawkish signals from the Fed. Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia President Anna Paulson said on Thursday the Fed will need to raise interest rates again because inflation is too high, while Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said the evidence did not suggest inflation was heading back to 2% on its own.

"The debate now is not really about whether the Federal Reserve will raise rates in December, but how much it will raise rates by," said Carol Kong, currency strategist at Commonwealth Bank of Australia.

"We still think 25 basis points is more likely," Kong said. "If they really want to quicken the pace of tightening, I think they will prefer to increase rates by 25 bps in consecutive meetings rather than deliver a bigger-than-usual hike."

YEN FIRMS ON INFLATION DATA

The yen firmed 0.4% against the dollar to 159.07 and is set to close the week with a small gain after three weeks of losses that had dragged the currency near the key 160 level.

Japan's annual core inflation accelerated to 2.2% in October, staying above the central bank's 2% target for a second straight month and pointing to broadening price pressures that strengthen the case for a near-term rate hike by the Bank of Japan.

Analysts at Capital Economics argue the yen's recent weakness is unlikely to last. With long-term inflation expectations now around target, further increases in yields would be mostly in real terms, which, combined with their view that US yields will fall, should prove yen-positive, the analysts said.

The Bank of Japan will likely raise interest rates for the third time this year at its December meeting and follow up with another by end-March, according to a ​majority of economists in a Reuters poll.

Sterling languished near a one-year low against the dollar at $1.3107, and the euro struggled near its lowest level since April 2025 and last bought $1.0971.

China's offshore yuan firmed 0.3% to 6.6762 per dollar, bouncing from a more than one-month low against the US dollar that it hit a day earlier as corporate repatriation offset the impact of a continuing dollar rally. China left key benchmark lending rates unchanged in November for an 18th consecutive month.

(Reporting by Li Gu in Shanghai and Rae Wee in Singapore, additional reporting by Sophie Kiderlin,;Editing by Tom Hogue and Sharon Singleton)

data.title: Fed's Paulson backs further rate hikes, says shared understanding beats guidance
data.description:
NEW YORK, Nov 19 (Reuters) - Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia President Anna Paulson said on Thursday the Fed will need to raise interest rates again because inflation is too high, while arguing that shared understanding matters more than explicit guidance on the rate outlook.

For the Fed, "understanding matters more than the specific ways we communicate," Paulson said in a speech delivered before a gathering held by the Money Marketeers of New York University.

"When we understand each other, we don't need to say as much when new data arrive," she said, adding, "You can anticipate how we'll respond, and we can act in ways that are steady and, for the most part, predictable."

Paulson's views on Fed communications come as the central bank has been overhauling how it explains its actions to the public. Under new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, the Fed has shortened its Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) policy statement and has launched a special task force to weigh how the Fed should communicate its actions and views.

At the same time, Warsh has, in contrast to other recent Fed leaders, stepped almost entirely away from providing any guidance about the interest-rate outlook.

But even as Warsh has pulled back, many of his colleagues on the central bank have continued to provide regular updates on where they think interest-rate policy is heading and how the economy is faring.

Paulson said after her formal remarks that the Fed will need to raise rates again because inflation is too high in an otherwise robust economy.

"I see growth that's strengthened and I see a labor market being at full employment, and so it's clear that inflation needs to be ... the priority" of monetary policymaking right now, Paulson said after her formal remarks.

"The way we bring inflation down is by having higher rates," she said, adding that there is "more tightening to do."

Paulson also said that slow and steady rate rises rather than dramatic action give the economy time to adjust to the increase in short-term borrowing costs.

Paulson holds a vote on the FOMC this year. The committee, which sets interest rates, is widely expected to raise its target rate of between 3.75% and 4% at the meeting scheduled for December 8-9.

Paulson said in her remarks that understanding how the Fed reacts to incoming data is particularly important.

"Communication works best when it builds a shared understanding of the reaction function, and that credibility is essential, because people act on messages they trust," she said.

Paulson said an understanding of what the Fed is doing and why helped markets navigate the Fed's decision to hold rates steady in late October, after boosting them in September while signaling more hikes were in the works.

"In October, markets expected further tightening, so the pause did not leave policy behind where it needed to be," she said.

"A shared understanding of the reaction function allowed policy to move deliberately and gave people time to adjust, without the risk that a pause was mistaken for a stop."

(Reporting by Michael S. Derby in New York; Editing by Matthew Lewis and Tom Hogue)

data.title: US AI chip curbs hit China tech stocks, spur self-sufficiency push
data.description:
SHANGHAI, Nov 20 (Reuters) - A flurry of US measures targeting China's access to advanced AI chips further pummelled Chinese technology stocks this week, as investors weigh whether Washington's latest curbs will slow Beijing's ambitions or accelerate its drive for technological self-sufficiency.

Chinese technology firms faced a series of new pressures, including US restrictions targeting Chinese firms' remote access to advanced AI chips, Nvidia's suspension of some chip shipments to China, a shareholder lawsuit against Alibaba and a US proposal that could require American companies to disclose their use of Chinese AI models.

Together, the developments show how the US-China contest for leadership in artificial intelligence is moving beyond semiconductor exports to cloud computing, software and corporate disclosure.

"Closing the gap at the leading edge before 2028, or even by 2030, looks difficult," Neil Shah, vice president of research at Counterpoint Research, said of the impact of US measures on China's AI industry.

The impact would be "far more prominent" in frontier model training than in inference, Shah said, adding that AI startups such as Moonshot AI, Z.AI, MiniMax and DeepSeek were more likely to be hit harder than hyperscalers such as Alibaba and Tencent.

Shares in leading Chinese tech companies have slumped since last week after Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang, who has pushed to preserve access to the Chinese market, resigned as CEO following reports that he had extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy.

Z.AI has tumbled 22% and MiniMax 34% over the last two weeks.

NEAR-TERM HIT

As Washington tightens curbs on access to advanced computing power, Chinese companies are racing to build a domestic AI ecosystem less dependent on US technology.

Executives at Tencent and Alibaba, two of China's biggest AI companies, said during earnings calls this week that the latest US restrictions would tighten computing constraints, though they differed on the near-term impact.

Tencent said its cloud business would be largely unaffected because its AI services rely mainly on inference workloads that can run on domestic chips.

But its President Martin Lau said the US restrictions would slow development of Tencent's next-generation AI model in the near term and accelerate China's shift towards domestic chips.

Alibaba CEO Eddie Wu also said the new US rule would affect its products and services next year, and could force the company to lower its long-term target of building 20 gigawatts of computing capacity.

While Alibaba maintained its long-term goal of generating $100 billion in external cloud revenue by 2030, cloud revenue growth was likely to slow to 30% to 45% next year from 53% in the latest quarter, as the company adjusts to the restrictions, it said.

"If (AI) training cycles become longer or the deployment of additional computing capacity slows, product iteration and commercialization could be delayed," said Liu Xingliang, a Beijing-based independent technology industry analyst.

DOMESTIC ALTERNATIVES

Both companies said domestic chips would play a growing role in meeting their computing needs. But China's capacity to manufacture advanced chips remains limited, with US export controls on ASML's immersion lithography machines and other tools limiting expansion.

Iluvatar CoreX, which supplies chips to ByteDance, said in a statement on its official WeChat account on Friday that it had built close ties with domestic semiconductor supply-chain partners to safeguard supplies, seeking to ease market concerns that had sent its shares down 17%.

Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corp, China's top contract chip manufacturer, is widely regarded as the only Chinese foundry producing advanced chips at scale using a 7-nanometer process. Much of that capacity has been earmarked for Huawei's Ascend AI chips, while Hua Hong Semiconductor's capacity to make advanced chips remains relatively limited.

Alibaba's Wu said the market remained supply-constrained and that domestic computing capacity would become "the primary engine supporting cloud revenue growth."

The restrictions are also rippling through overseas suppliers. Following new US licensing requirements announced this week on overseas data centres serving Chinese AI companies, Taiwan's ​TSMC suspended some previously permitted advanced chip manufacturing orders from Chinese customers, Reuters reported on Thursday.

(Reporting by Casey Hall in Shanghai and Sophie Yu in Beijing; Additional reporting by Pan Che and Xiuyuan Ning; Editing by Miyoung Kim and Tom Hogue)

data.title: Taiwan's Stock Pickers Are Walking Out to Bet Their Own Money
data.description:
NEW YORK, Oct. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Fly On Wall Street News Commentary - Taiwan's benchmark stock index was up 62% this year, the best showing of any major equity gauge in the world, when Bloomberg reported on Oct. 16 that some of the island's professional fund managers and analysts are quitting their jobs to invest their own money. Strict rules keep them from trading the very stocks they pick for clients, and in a year when about one in ten stocks in the index has more than doubled, some have decided the trade-off is no longer worth it. Companies and funds mentioned in this article include: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited ( TSM ) [TSMC] , ASE Technology Holding Co., Ltd. ( ASX ) [ASE] , United Microelectronics Corporation ( UMC ) [UMC] , iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF , The Taiwan Fund, Inc. ( TWN ) .

Watching From Behind the Locker

Taiwan does not ban personal investing outright, but its asset-management code of conduct bars staff from trading a locally listed stock or a linked derivative within seven business days before or after their firm's funds trade it, which in practice rules out personal stock-picking. Fund managers must also lock away their phones, laptops and smartwatches each morning until the market closes at 1:30 p.m. The phone rule was formalized in 2024 to deter insider trading, the Taipei Times reported in July, after six former fund managers from four firms were indicted for front-running trades through the accounts of relatives and friends.

Ken Tsai, 40, a fund manager who until July worked at a large Taiwanese asset manager that Bloomberg did not name, told Bloomberg he made a Taiwanese maker of AI-server data-transfer components his fund's largest holding in 2024. The stock rose more than fivefold in 2025 and about sixfold again this year, but he owned none of it personally. "It left me with a strong sense of relative deprivation," he said. He now works at a private investment firm in Taipei, which was also not named. Pay adds to the pull: Taiwan portfolio managers earn roughly US$124,000 to US$311,000 a year, well below Hong Kong base salaries, according to Bloomberg, citing headhunters and recruitment-firm data.

The private shops they are joining sit outside those rules. They register as private companies with the Ministry of Economic Affairs and do not need asset-management licenses from the Financial Supervisory Commission because they do not raise public money. Brokers told Bloomberg some of them now generate more than NT$10 billion in monthly trading volume, rivaling mid-sized asset managers.

The Rally Behind the Exits

Much of the rally traces back to the AI hardware supply chain. TSMC reported third-quarter revenue of NT$1.49 trillion (US$46.7 billion) on Oct. 15, up 50.9% from a year earlier, while net income jumped 68.7% and gross margin reached 66.4%. It guided fourth-quarter revenue from US$52.3 billion to US$54.3 billion.

Chip packaging and testing has ridden the same wave. ASE Technology ( ASX ) reported September net revenue of NT$88.1 billion, up 45.5% from a year earlier, and third-quarter revenue of NT$244.2 billion, up 44.8%.

Mature-node foundry UMC reported August sales up 30.71% from a year earlier, lifting year-to-date sales 14.66%. In its second-quarter report, the company guided for capacity utilization above 90% in the third quarter and said revenue from its 22/28nm business continues to set record highs.

CONTINUED... Read more market coverage at: flyonwallstreet.com

A Talent Squeeze, Not a Stampede

The numbers point to churn more than an exodus. Fewer than half of Taiwan's 20 largest local equity mutual funds have kept the same portfolio manager for more than three years, according to fund-data site MoneyDJ, and Bloomberg reported that applications for junior roles at some international firms have roughly halved this year. Yet the FSC said the industry's registered headcount actually rose to 4,729 in September from 4,581 at the end of 2025. Firms are responding: the largest foreign asset manager in Taiwan is offering cross-market analyst roles and office rotations to keep staff.

Regulators are paying attention. The FSC said on Oct. 15 it is gathering information and plans to review the rules, balancing market development against conflicts of interest and investor protection. One asset-management executive told Bloomberg there is no easy solution for now.

The Case for the Pros

At least one professionally managed fund has kept pace. The Taiwan Fund ( TWN ), a closed-end fund listed in New York, reported a 47.36% total return for its fiscal quarter ended May 31, against 26.12% for the TAIEX Total Return Index over the same period, with net asset value of US$116.90 a share at the end of that quarter.

Investors who prefer to own the whole market can use the iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF, which holds about US$11.9 billion in assets.

Last week was a reminder of how quickly the math can change. The TAIEX fell 4.6%, its first weekly decline in five weeks, as a technology selloff spread and TSMC CEO C.C. Wei warned of macroeconomic uncertainty and weak consumer demand, according to Trading Economics. In New York, TSMC's shares fell 8.98% from the Oct. 9 close to $412.61 on Oct. 16, ASE dropped 14.86% to $39.53, UMC slid 13.68% to $19.82, the iShares fund lost 7.04% to $106.26 and The Taiwan Fund ( TWN ) declined 8.78% to $94.18, according to Stock Analysis data. For the managers who just traded a salary for their own account, those swings now land on them.

data.title: California AG subpoenas Nvidia over concerns about former CEO, China ties
data.description:
Nov 19 (Reuters) - California Attorney General Rob Bonta said on Thursday his office had served an investigative subpoena to Nvidia ( NVDA ) related to reports of former CEO Jensen Huang's alleged affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy.

"The conduct of Nvidia ( NVDA ) and its former CEO raises bright red flags," Bonta said, adding that his office was examining whether Nvidia ( NVDA ) or Huang's actions resulted in China obtaining advanced chips or confidential information, and if the company misled investors and the public about the risk.

The probe will help determine whether Nvidia's ( NVDA ) actions violated California law, the attorney general's office said.

Huang resigned last week after revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang and two with Nvidia ( NVDA ) employees.

US intelligence agencies are trying to determine the extent of Alice Huang's ties to China's Ministry of State Security and what information she may have passed to Beijing, according to Reuters.

China has rejected allegations of an espionage operation targeting Jensen Huang.

Nvidia's ( NVDA ) board has ruled out bringing Jensen Huang back as CEO, despite a campaign by employees and prominent technology figures, including Elon Musk, to reinstate him.

The US Securities and Exchange Commission is also reportedly probing Nvidia ( NVDA ) after Huang's resignation.

The House Foreign Affairs Committee said on Thursday that the Trump administration had approved shipments of nearly 900,000 advanced Nvidia ( NVDA ) and AMD AI chips to Chinese companies between December 2025 and May this year, although it was unclear how many were ultimately shipped.

Nvidia ( NVDA ) said the approvals were subject to strict conditions and limited volumes and that it had stopped shipping H200 chips to China.

(Reporting by Harshita Mary Varghese in Bengaluru; Editing by Shinjini Ganguli)

data.title: EMERGING MARKETS-AI selloff drives Taiwan to worst week since 1990, rattles Asia markets
data.description:
* Taiwan index has lost 17.5% so far this week
    * TSMC, MediaTek, Samsung, SK Hynix ( SKHY ) slide
    * MSCI EM Asia eyes worst week since 2020
    * Indonesian rupiah hovers near record lows

    (Updates for afternoon trade)
    By Rajasik Mukherjee
       Nov 20 (Reuters) - Taiwan stocks tumbled more than 6% on
Friday and clocked their worst week in more than three decades
as investors unwound AI-related bets over concerns around
valuations, profitability and rising debt.
    Taiwan's benchmark equity index ended 6.2% down to
hit its lowest close since mid-April, deepening its weekly loss
to 17.5%, the steepest five-day rout since 1990.
    The index has lost $1.12 trillion in value since October 6,
when it touched an all-time high, according to LSEG-compiled
data. Over that period, it has lost nearly 28% as of Friday's
close.
    Stocks in South Korea fell more than 5% to their
lowest point in more than nine months, with Samsung Electronics ( SSNLF )
 and SK Hynix ( SKHY ) shedding 7% each.
    That pushed the MSCI EM Asia equity index
down more than 4% to levels last seen in early April. The gauge
has lost nearly 9% this week, putting it on course for its worst
week since mid-March 2020.
    The weakness spread to Southeast Asian equity markets:
stocks in Thailand and Singapore fell around 2%
each, while those in the Philippines dived more than 3%
to their weakest level since April 2020.
    Regional currencies also came under pressure due to foreign
selling: the Indonesian rupiah hovered near a record low
of 18,285 per US dollar, while the Philippine peso and
the Korean won edged lower.
    "There's a knock-on effect in Asia," said Dilin Wu, research
strategist at Pepperstone.
    "When foreign investors sell local shares and move their
money back into dollars, that puts additional pressure on
regional currencies."


    WHEN THE CHIPS ARE DOWN
    The AI trade has been hit by concerns over valuations,
rising debt, growing opposition to data centres and the fallout
from Jensen Huang's departure from chipmaker Nvidia ( NVDA ),
sparking an aggressive unwinding of crowded positions.
    Even Anthropic's record-breaking IPO, followed by a debut
that fizzled later in the session on Thursday, did not spark a
broader rally.
    That caution reverberated in Asia, as investors sold
chipmakers in Taiwan and South Korea, key beneficiaries of the
global AI trade.
    TSMC, the world's largest contract chipmaker and a
key Nvidia ( NVDA ) supplier, hit a more than seven-month low by dropping
as much as 6.2%, and logged its worst week since October 1997.
Shares of chip designer MediaTek dropped 10%.
     "The selloff is partly about AI valuations, but the scale
of the decline tells us there's more going on," Wu added.
     "Even Nvidia's ( NVDA ) blockbuster earnings haven't been enough to
reassure investors about the sustainability of AI spending ...
add foreign selling and margin calls to the mix, and the decline
can quickly feed on itself."

data.title: Japan's Nikkei ends 5% lower as Anthropic's IPO fails to restore AI confidence
data.description:
(Updates with closing prices)

By Junko Fujita

TOKYO, Nov 20 (Reuters) - Japan's Nikkei stock average fell 5% to close at a seven-month low on Friday, as technology shares tumbled after Anthropic's IPO failed to restore confidence in the AI trade.

The Nikkei ended 5.06% lower at 56,436.65, its lowest close since April 13. For the week, the index lost 7.7%.

The broader Topix fell 3.88% to 3,674.22.

"There was a high expectation that Anthropic's market debut may lift sentiment for AI-related shares, but that hope faded as its price pared gains," said Hiroyuki Ueno, chief strategist at Sumitomo Mitsui Trust Asset Management.

Shares of Anthropic, the world's first publicly traded frontier AI company, opened 34% higher than the $83 IPO price set on Wednesday. But the stock pared gains and closed at $97.17, up 17% from its IPO price.

In Japan, chip-related Advantest ( ADTTF ) and Tokyo Electron ( TOELF ) slid 10.32% and 7.06%, respectively. Technology investor SoftBank Group tumbled 14.48% and memory chip maker Kioxia ( KXHCF ) lost 11.66%.

"Investors realise that these chip shares became cheap, but they are afraid to pick them up because they are afraid there may be another dip in the market," said Ueno.

Of 225 stocks on the Nikkei, 214 fell and 11 rose.

Among the advancers were insurer Tokio Marine Holdings ( TKOMF ) , which rose 2.03%. Peers MS&AD Insurance and Sompo Holdings ( NHOLF ) rose 0.4% and 2.01%, respectively.

Railway operators rose, with Keisei Electric Railway ( KELRF ) and Odakyu Electric Railway ( ODERF ) edging up 0.26% and 0.08%, respectively.

Takeda Pharmaceutical ( TAK ) rose 0.33%.

Of more than 1,500 stocks trading on the Tokyo Stock Exchange's prime market, 93% fell, 5% rose and 1% traded flat.

(Reporting by Junko Fujita; Editing by Rashmi Aich and Ronojoy Mazumdar)
